title: Whatever the Body Can Reach
logline: A shallow brackish lagoon of about seventeen square kilometres, whose single mouth the sea seals with sand once the rains stop, and which then spends months going down; as it goes down, birds of thirty different builds work the same few inches of the same water, and no two of them can take the same thing out of it.
human_question: Two creatures are standing in the same water. What makes it not the same water?

place.what_kind_of_place: A shallow estuarine lagoon on a low, thinly settled stretch of the north-east coast, roughly seventeen square kilometres of brackish water no more than four metres deep anywhere and ankle-deep over most of its area. It is fed by small seasonal rivers off the dry-zone plain behind it and joined to the sea by one narrow channel at its southern end, which a sand bar closes for much of the year. Behind the water there is scrub, dry forest, paddy and coconut; along the margins there are mangrove and seagrass beds and long bars of firm sand; and three small settlements sit on its shores. When the mouth is shut, the lagoon becomes a closed, slowly shrinking dish of water in a very large flat landscape.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because as the water drops it sorts everything living in it into layers, and the sorting is visible from the air. At first light the whole lagoon is a single sheet with the sky in it. Over weeks, bars surface, channels narrow, and the birds distribute themselves along the new edges strictly by what their bodies can do: the long bills in the deep margin, the short ones on the wet sand, the divers where there is still a channel, the waders in between, all of them within a few metres of one another and none of them in the same world. At ground level it is a film of single actions repeated thousands of times: one bill, one inch of water, one thing taken. The biggest shot the place gives, which is the whole shallow dish from directly above with the birds written across it in bands, is also the clearest statement of the concept.
place.what_moves_or_changes: The bar, the level, the salinity and the birds, none of them under anyone's control. The bar closes after the rains and is worked at by the sea and by whatever comes down the rivers. The level falls week by week and the water gets saltier as it falls. Species arrive, hold for a period and go. Nothing here can be scheduled beyond the hour and the tide, and what the film gets on any given morning is whatever the lagoon is doing that week.
place.when_it_looks_best: The months after the north-east rains stop and the mouth closes, when the level has begun to fall and the bars are appearing; and the very early morning, when the water is flat enough to hold the sky and the light is low enough to separate the birds from their own reflections. A second, harder window is the first heavy rain, when the level comes up and the whole arrangement is undone in a few days.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about a shallow lagoon going down through a dry season, and about what lives in the last of it. The bar across the mouth, the sheet of water at dawn, the bars surfacing, the bands of birds, the enormous flat light, the mangrove edge, the small settlements at the rim, and then the rain that takes it all back. It has its own complete shape with nothing said over it, and anyone who likes water, birds or very large empty light has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same weeks become two things the sources say that nobody expects. First, that the result of a good act is not a payment at all: what arrives during a life is a set of single resultant moments of consciousness, one agreeable sight or sound or taste at a time, and the sources list sixteen ways in which where you were born, what body you have, what time you live in and what you actually do will let a result in or shut it out. Second, that for animals the plane is not a place anywhere; it is the kind of body a being is born into. A lagoon full of different bills, each of them able to reach exactly one depth, is where both of those stop being abstractions. The voice never says that any creature in frame is an instance of anything, and says so out loud.

sequence.on_screen: Dawn, very high and straight down. A pale flat sheet filling most of the frame, dry country around it, and at the southern end a clean line of sand lying across the only gap to the sea.
sequence.voice: The sea shut this at the end of the rains. From now until the next ones there is one dish of water here, with no way in and no way out, and it will spend the next few months getting smaller and saltier.

sequence.on_screen: Lower, tracking along a margin: sand bars newly out of the water, and along the wet edge of each, birds standing in bands. Tall ones behind, small ones in front, all within a few metres.
sequence.voice: The sources divide the places a being can be born into four, and the first of them is called apāya, which they take apart to mean simply gone away from aya, from happiness [C051-P:L35–L40; C051-P:L46–L51]. But when they get to animals they say something unexpectedly flat. Animals have no place set aside for them [C051-P:L87]. The animal kind is itself the animal plane [C051-M:L11–L13; C051-P:L103].

sequence.on_screen: Ground level, very close, held long. Four or five different bills working the same inch of water within a body length of each other: one long and curved, one straight and short, one flat, one spoon-ended.
sequence.voice: So the plane is not somewhere else. It is the shape you are working with. These birds are standing in one inch of one lagoon, and not one of them can reach what the bird beside it is reaching. The film is not saying that any creature here is an example of anything, and the sources do not license anybody to say where any being has come from or is going.

sequence.on_screen: A single feeding action isolated and held: the head goes down, something is taken, the head comes up. Then again. Then again, at the same interval, for a long time.
sequence.voice: Now the harder claim, from the chapter on what a good act actually produces. Not a lump sum. During a life, what it gives are particular resultant states of mind, sixteen of them counted, arising one at a time as an agreeable thing is actually met [C059-P:L394; C059-M:L9]. A result, in this analysis, is one moment of contact and then it is over. That is the whole of what is on offer, and it looks like this.

sequence.on_screen: Time passing: the same margin over several weeks. The water lower each time. A bar that was a shallow becomes dry sand. Birds that were there are not there. The remaining ones crowded into a shrinking wet edge.
sequence.voice: And the sources are blunt that having done the good is not enough by itself. They set out sixteen ways in which a result is let in or shut out, turning on four things: the existence you were born into, what body you got, what time you are living in, and whether you do the right thing at the right moment [C059-P:L303–L323; C059-P:L351–L361]. Which is not a way of saying that whatever happens to anyone was deserved. It is the opposite. It is a list of the ways real goodness can fail to land.

sequence.on_screen: Last light on still water at the mangrove edge; the settlements as small lines of roof on the far rim; almost no movement.
sequence.voice: The same chapter breaks an act of giving into three moments, not one: the getting ready, the letting go, and the going back over it afterwards, and it says the state of the first and third is part of the strength of the second [C059-P:L45–L49]. It also says something people find counter-intuitive: how the act felt does not decide how its result will feel [C059-M:L11]. You are not building the weather of your own future mood.

sequence.on_screen: The bar across the mouth again from height at the very end of the light, the lagoon behind it almost black. No commentary over the final minute.
sequence.voice: One thing this group has to say plainly before it goes any further. The word the sources use for one class of unhappy beings, peta, is used loosely elsewhere for the dead, and the Margaya separates the two: in this chapter it means a particular class of suffering beings and nothing else [C051-M:L15]. So nothing here is about anybody who has died. Nobody is being placed anywhere. What the water shows is narrower and stranger than that: a result is one moment of meeting something, and what you can meet is decided by the body you are doing it with.

concept_merge.why_together: C059 supplies the claim and C051 supplies the condition on it, and a drying lagoon is the one place where both are literal. C059 holds that what a wholesome sense-sphere action gives during a life is not a reward but a set of resultant consciousnesses, counted at sixteen, arising as agreeable objects are actually met [C059-P:L394; C059-M:L9]; that an act has a before, a letting go and an after, and the first and third reach back into the second [C059-P:L45–L49]; that the feeling of the act does not determine the feeling of the result [C059-M:L11]; and that sixteen configurations of destiny, body, time and effort decide whether any of it gets through at all [C059-P:L303–L323; C059-P:L351–L361]. C051 then says the thing that makes the second half of that list concrete rather than moralising: animals have no plane set aside for them anywhere, and the kind of body is itself the plane [C051-P:L87; C051-M:L11–L13; C051-P:L103]. Put on a shrinking sheet of water where a hundred kinds of bill are working within a few metres of one another, 'the body decides what can be received' stops being a doctrine and becomes the thing the drone is looking at.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That a result, in this analysis, has no size and no lump form; it is one moment of contact, and the equipment doing the contacting is not something anybody chose. C059 on its own becomes a sermon about giving, which is exactly what this group must not make in the weeks after somebody's death. C051 on its own is a cosmology that the digest warns is dangerous to film at all. Together on this water they make a single, sober, checkable point, and they make it about bodies and depths rather than about anybody's fate. The old version of this idea got the same concepts from a family's seventh-day almsgiving for a dead relative. This one gets them from a lagoon, which cannot be bereaved, cannot be asked to perform its faith, and is not anybody's grief.

concept_links.why: The film uses the digest's account of what a result actually is, and its account of what blocks one. Wholesome sense-sphere action produces rebirth-linking in the happy sense-sphere planes and, during the course of a life, the sixteen resultant minds that arise as objects are met [C059-P:L394; C059-M:L9]; an act of giving is divided into the intention while preparing, the intention at the moment of letting go, and the intention afterwards, with the surrounding states deciding the strength of the act [C059-P:L45–L49]; and the sixteen-fold scheme turns on favourable or unfavourable destiny, body, time and effort [C059-P:L303–L323; C059-P:L351–L361]. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is kept, and several are spoken. The film never offers 'do good and good things will happen to you', because the whole fifth beat is the sources' own list of how goodness fails to land. It never says that what happens to anyone was deserved. Critically, the digest's own examples inside that scheme are congenital blindness and other disability [C059-P:L343–L349; C059-P:L381; C059-P:L407], and those lines are deliberately not cited, not paraphrased and not narrated anywhere: no disabled person appears in this film and no bodily difference in any human being is offered as an instance of anything. The Margaya's point that the pleasant feeling of an act does not decide the feeling of its result is used as a corrective [C059-M:L11]. The ranking of recipients, the giving stories, the Brahma lifespans, the 'favourable effort' examples of well-timed theft and bribery, and above all the material on sharing merit with the dead, are all absent from the film.

Linked for exactly three of the digest's statements, all of which are safe to film and none of which comments on any person. First, the four planes and the source's own unpacking of apāya as departed from happiness [C051-P:L35–L40; C051-P:L46–L51]. Second, the flat statement that animals have no place set aside for them [C051-P:L87] and that the animal kind is itself the animal plane [C051-M:L11–L13; C051-P:L103], which is the sentence the whole location was chosen for. Third, the Margaya's own separation of peta from 'the dead' [C051-M:L15], spoken aloud so that a group of films about endings cannot be heard to say where anybody has gone. The digest's warnings are the reason for everything else being left out. The hells, their causes and their lifespans are not narrated. The source ties congenital blindness to a kind of rebirth-consciousness, and that passage is not used, not implied, and not present in any form; no disabled person appears in this group. The source names livelihoods, including those who kill cattle, goats and chickens, and links them to particular destinations, and that material is not used here and is not allowed anywhere near the settlements at this lagoon or the people who work its water. Nothing in the film suggests that any creature in frame is the rebirth of anybody, or that any person who has died is in any plane at all.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That in this analysis the result of a good act is not a quantity that is owed and paid, but a series of single moments of meeting something agreeable, each of which is over as soon as it happens; and that whether any of them can occur at all depends on the equipment and the circumstances a being finds itself with. And that the sources' talk of planes, at least for animals, is not talk about places somewhere else.
what_must_be_real: The lagoon's own timetable, the birds' own behaviour and the people of the three settlements' own use of the water. No bird is baited, flushed, called, driven, lit or approached to make a shot, and no hide is placed where it will keep birds off water in a month when the water is scarce. Nothing is fed. The drone is flown high enough and infrequently enough that it does not move a roost or a feeding flock, and if it does, it stops. The households on the shores are filmed only with consent and are never framed as an example of anything, least of all of the sources' material on livelihoods and destinations, which is excluded from this film entirely. No person who has died is mentioned, referred to or implied anywhere in it.
position_hint: middle: it needs the viewer to have already accepted that the series is describing mechanisms rather than pronouncing on people, because it is the only film in the group that goes near the planes at all, and it hands on the question of what conditions let a result through. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Letting any creature in frame be read as an instance of a plane, a destination or somebody's rebirth, which the digests forbid and a camera cannot show.
Letting the animal realm's place in the woeful planes come across as contempt for the animals on screen, or as pity dressed up as doctrine.
Repeating, paraphrasing or even implying the sources' use of congenital blindness and disability as examples inside the sixteen-fold scheme. No disabled person appears anywhere in this group.
Letting the sources' list of livelihoods and their destinations touch the settlements at the lagoon or anyone who works its water.
Turning C059 into 'do good and good things will happen to you', or into its cruel inverse, that what happens to someone shows what they deserved.
Disturbing birds for footage in the weeks when the water is at its lowest and the cost of being moved is highest.
Making a beautiful drying-out into a film that quietly celebrates a hard season for the people and animals living through it.
drop_if: The bar does not close, or the season is wet enough that the lagoon never draws down, so the sorting the film is built on never happens.
Filming cannot be done without moving birds off water in a month when they cannot afford it.
The settlements on the shores do not want a crew or a drone over the lagoon.
Permissions for flight over a coastal water body in this area cannot be obtained, or the area is restricted.

connections.note: Two films about what a set of conditions will and will not let through: one sorted up the side of a mountain, one sorted across four inches of water.
The other film in the group that touches the planes, and the two need to agree exactly on what they refuse to claim about anybody.
Both watch conditions rather than agents decide an outcome over a whole landscape.

selection.reason: It gives both concepts a home that cannot be bereaved, and the one shot the location produces, the shallow dish from above with the birds written across it in bands, is also the clearest statement of the concept.

review.note: Rewritten 2026-09-23 into the footage-led shape. What was dropped: the entire old subject, in which a bereaved household cooked through the night and held a seventh-day almsgiving in a dead relative's name while the camera watched them pour water and say the name aloud. It filmed real bereavement and a real funerary rite, it made hosts and mourners of the same exhausted people, and the C061 digest states that these extracts do not discuss funeral and memorial customs and should not be made to comment on them. The merit-sharing material in C059, which was the old film's entire mechanism, has been dropped with the subject and is not used anywhere in the new film. C059 was rebuilt around what the digest says a result actually is and around the sixteen circumstances that let one through, with the disability examples inside that scheme deliberately excluded. C051 was kept but cut down to three statements that comment on nobody, including the Margaya's own separation of peta from the dead, which is now spoken on screen. Both digests were re-read from scratch and every citation checked against digest evidence rather than carried over from the old text.

suggested_location.name: Nayaru Lagoon and its sand bar, on the coast between Alampil and Kumulamunai

also_known_as.name: Nai Aru
also_known_as.meaning: the lagoon and the small river that feeds it

also_known_as.name: Nayaru
also_known_as.meaning: the common transliteration used locally and in travel writing

suggested_location.region: Mullaitivu District, Northern Province: the low, thinly settled coast running south from the district town, with the lagoon lying behind the beach between the settlements of Alampil, Chemmalai and Kumulamunai
suggested_location.why_here: Because the shape of the concept is the shape of the place. The lagoon is about seventeen and a half square kilometres and nowhere more than four metres deep, which means almost all of it is shallow enough for wading birds to stand in; it is fed by small seasonal rivers and joined to the sea by one narrow southern channel that a sand bar very often blocks, and the bar closes after the rains stop. A closed, shallow, brackish dish that then spends months going down is a machine for sorting animals by what their bodies can do, and it does the sorting in bands that only read from the air. The lagoon is reported to hold a wide variety of water birds, including ducks, gulls, terns and other shorebirds, in a setting of seagrass beds, mangrove, scrub, paddy and coconut. It is also, for the purposes of this group, a place where an ending can be filmed with nobody dying: what ends here is a season and a connection to the sea.
what_to_film: The whole lagoon from directly overhead at first light, high enough that the bands of birds along the margins read as bands and the bar across the mouth reads as a line.
The bar itself at several stages, from the sea side and the lagoon side, including whatever the last rains left of the channel.
One margin returned to repeatedly over several weeks at the same hour, so the drop in level and the change in who is standing there is a single continuous observation.
Very close, long-held ground work on bills of different lengths working the same few inches of water within a body length of one another.
A single feeding action isolated and repeated, filmed plainly and at length, as the film's picture of one moment of contact.
The bars surfacing: firm wet sand, drying sand, the wrack line, the tracks.
The mangrove and seagrass margins in flat light, and the very large empty light over the middle of the lagoon at both ends of the day.
The first heavy rain, if the schedule reaches it, and the whole arrangement coming undone in a few days.
suggested_location.access: By the coast road south from the district town, with the three shoreline settlements giving the practical access to the water. Everything depends on those communities: the lagoon is worked and lived on, and a crew and a drone need their agreement as well as any permission the coastal and aviation rules require. Parts of this coast carry security and unexploded-ordnance considerations that must be checked with the relevant authorities before anyone walks a margin. Bird work needs long lenses and patience rather than proximity, and no hide should be placed anywhere that keeps birds off water in a low month.
suggested_location.best_time: The dry months after the north-east monsoon, once the bar has closed and the level has begun to drop; and within a day, the first two hours of light, when the water is flat and the low sun separates the birds from their reflections. A shorter second window at the first heavy rain of the next season.

suggested_location.research_note: That the lagoon is estuarine and brackish, covers about 17.6 square kilometres, is at most four metres deep, is fed by a number of small rivers, is joined to the sea by one narrow southern channel that is very often blocked by a sand bar which closes after the rainy season, is fringed by mangrove and seagrass with dense scrub, paddy and coconut behind it, holds a wide variety of water birds including ducks, gulls, terns and other shorebirds, and has Alampil, Chemmalai and Kumulamunai on its shores, is all from the sources above and is desk research only. The coordinates are the lagoon's own, not a chosen margin or hide position. Nobody has been approached and no permission has been sought. The central premise of the sequence, that the drawdown sorts the birds into readable bands along the margins, is an inference from the lagoon's depth and closure behaviour and has not been observed or confirmed by anyone. Security, mine-clearance status and aviation restrictions on this stretch of coast are entirely unchecked. Both images are of the lagoon and one of its shore settlements in general views, not of the bar, the margins or any of the bird behaviour the film depends on.

unknowns: Whether the drawdown actually sorts the birds the way the film assumes. This is an inference from depth and closure behaviour and nobody has checked it; it is the question that decides whether the film exists.
When, and how reliably, the bar closes in any given year, and how far the level falls before the next rains.
What the security, access and unexploded-ordnance position is on this stretch of coast, and whether a drone can be flown over the lagoon at all.
Whether the three shoreline communities would want a crew there, and on what terms.
Whether bird work of the closeness the middle of the film needs can be done without moving birds off water in a low month. If it cannot, the film does not get made.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
